20a-13.citation: Utah Code Title 20A, Chapter 13 (Elections to Federal Offices), Part 3 (Presidential Electors), esp. 20A-13-301
20a-13.note: The chapter's own PDF, the 'PDF' link under 'Download Options' on the chapter's page.

ties.applies_to: a race in which two or more candidates for an office receive an equal and the highest number of votes (a general or other election; for a primary see the next rule); excludes a race run by instant runoff voting under the Municipal Alternate Voting Methods Pilot Project
ties.steps: (1) the election officer must conduct a recount of the race, no later than 10 calendar days after the board of canvassers certifies the vote totals (20A-4-401(2)(a), (5)(a)(i)); (2) if the recount still leaves a tie, the board of canvassers declares a 'tie vote' (20A-4-304(1)(b)); (3) the election officer determines the winning candidate by lot, in whatever manner the officer determines, in a public meeting held no later than the first business day that is at least three calendar days after the recount canvass is completed, with notice to each tied candidate and a chance to watch the drawing or send a representative (20A-1-304(2))
ties.who: the election officer (county clerk, municipal clerk, special district clerk, or the lieutenant governor for a statewide or multi-county race)

sources.quote: The election officer shall conduct a recount of votes cast in a race if: (a) two or more candidates for an office receive an equal and the highest number of votes for that office

if, after conducting a recount under Subsection 20A-4-401(5), a tie vote occurs, the election officer shall, in a public meeting held no later than the first business day that is at least three calendar days after the day on which the recount canvass is completed: (a) determine the winning candidate, by lot, in whatever manner the election officer determines

ties.note: The words are 'a race' and 'an office' without limit; 20A-4-401(4) and (6) name statewide, multi-county, county, municipal and special district races, so those are explicit. Federal and state legislative offices are not named separately and are read within 'an office' [inferred]. A tie in an at-large race (several seats) is handled by 20A-4-401(2)(b) and (5)(b)(iv)(D): a tie vote is declared only if a lot is needed to fill the last seat. Municipal charters and special-district law were not read.

ties.applies_to: county, municipal, school and special district offices decided under the same Title 20A sections
ties.steps: same two steps as the general rule above, with the election officer of the local government (county clerk, municipal clerk, special district clerk) conducting the recount and then drawing the lot

sources.quote: for all other elections, no later than 5 p.m. on the first business day that is at least three calendar days after the day on which the canvass is completed, with: [...] (i) the municipal clerk, if the election is a municipal general election; (ii) the special district clerk, if the election is a special district election; (iii) the county clerk, for a race voted on entirely within a single county

ties.note: Shown separately because the quoted words name the local filing officers for a requested recount; that the tie rule (20A-4-401(2), 20A-1-304(2)) reaches local offices is my reading of 'the election officer' and 'a race' [inferred]. State general law only; city and town charters and ordinances were not read.

ties.applies_to: a tie in a primary election race, after the recount
ties.steps: the recount required by 20A-4-401(2) comes first; then the lot is cast by whoever the statute names for the office: for a national, statewide or other office that represents more than one county, the governor, lieutenant governor and attorney general at a public meeting called by the governor; for a county office, the district court judges of the district; any other primary (for example a municipal primary) the election officer under 20A-1-304(2). Each meeting is held no later than the first business day at least three calendar days after the recount canvass, with notice and a chance for each tied candidate to observe
ties.who: the governor, lieutenant governor and attorney general (national, statewide or multi-county office); the district court judges (county office); otherwise the election officer

sources.quote: a tie vote occurs in a primary election race for a national, statewide, or other office that represents more than one county, the governor, lieutenant governor, and attorney general shall, at a public meeting called by the governor [...] determine the winning nominee, by lot, in whatever manner the governor determines
a tie vote occurs in a primary election race for a county office, the district court judges of the district in which the county is located shall, at a public meeting called by the judges

ties.note: 20A-1-304(2) begins 'Except as provided in Subsection (3)', so subsection (3) displaces the election officer for these two classes of primary. A state legislative primary in a single county is not named in (3); it falls to subsection (2) or, if the district spans counties, to (3)(a) as 'other office that represents more than one county' [inferred].

ties.applies_to: the vote for President and Vice President, which elects the presidential electors
ties.steps: the statute says only that the highest number of votes elects the electors; no tie provision for the presidential vote was found

sources.quote: The highest number of votes cast for candidates for president and vice president of the United States elects the presidential electors for:

ties.note: An absence, marked inferred. I read all of 20A-13 Part 3 (Presidential Electors, sections 301 to 304), and the tie sections 20A-4-401 and 20A-1-304, which speak of candidates 'for an office'. Whether they reach the presidential vote is not stated. Other chapters of Title 20A (for example 20A-9, 20A-5) were not searched for a presidential tie rule.

ties.applies_to: any ballot proposition submitted to voters
ties.steps: an equal number of yes and no votes means the proposition fails (no lot, no new election)

sources.quote: Any ballot proposition submitted to voters for their approval or rejection: [...] fails if: (i) the number of "yes" votes equal the number of "no" votes

ties.note: The resolution is neither lot nor new election: the tie decides the measure against passing. A request for a recount of a measure is separate (see recounts).

threshold.in_words: a recount with no request happens when two or more candidates for an office receive an equal and the highest number of votes (or, in an at-large race, an equal number of votes where one of them must be eliminated to fill the offices)

recounts.cost_bearer: the state for a statewide or multi-county race; otherwise the political subdivision that conducts the election (or that contracted with a provider election officer to run it)

sources.quote: The election officer shall conduct a recount of votes cast in a race if: (a) two or more candidates for an office receive an equal and the highest number of votes for that office

The cost of a recount under Subsection (5) shall be paid by: (a) for a statewide race or multi-county race, the state; or (b) for all other races: (i) the political subdivision that conducts the election

recounts.note: A recount that occurs only on a tie. The election officer recounts all ballots cast in the race and re-examines uncounted ballots; a tie that remains goes to the lot (see ties). Does not apply to a race run by instant runoff voting (pilot project).

threshold.percent_of: the total number of votes cast for all candidates in the race
threshold.conditions: the one-vote alternative applies only where the total of all votes cast in the race is 400 or less
threshold.in_words: a margin between the winning and the losing candidate equal to or less than one-quarter of one percent of all votes cast for all candidates in the race, or exactly one vote where 400 votes or fewer were cast in the race

who_may_request: the losing candidate, by a request filed no later than 5 p.m. on the first business day that is at least three calendar days after the canvass is completed, with the municipal clerk, special district clerk, county clerk, or the lieutenant governor (statewide or multi-county race)
recounts.cost_bearer: the state for a statewide or multi-county race; otherwise the political subdivision that conducts the election (no cost to the candidate)

sources.quote: for a race between candidates, if the difference between the number of votes cast for a winning candidate in the race and a losing candidate in the race is equal to or less than .25% of the total number of votes cast for all candidates in the race, the losing candidate may file a request for a recount

for a race between candidates where the total of all votes cast in the race is 400 or less, if the difference between the number of votes cast for a winning candidate in the race and a losing candidate in the race is one vote, the losing candidate may file a request for a recount

recounts.note: The recount is held within seven calendar days after the request. Utah has no recount that a candidate may buy beyond this margin in 20A-4-401 (the whole section was read). 'Equal to or less than' makes the .25% boundary inclusive. The cost rule is subsection (6), which covers a recount 'under Subsection (5)', that is the tie recount and the requested candidate recount.

threshold.percent_of: the total votes cast for or against the proposition
threshold.conditions: the one-vote alternative applies only where the total of all votes cast for or against the proposition is 400 or less
threshold.in_words: the proposition passes or fails by a margin equal to or less than one-quarter of one percent of the total votes cast for or against it, or by exactly one vote where 400 or fewer votes were cast

who_may_request: any 10 voters who voted in the election where the proposition was on the ballot, filing no later than 5 p.m. on the first business day that is at least seven calendar days after the canvass, with the municipal clerk, special district clerk, county clerk or lieutenant governor

sources.quote: for a ballot proposition or a bond proposition, if the proposition passes or fails by a margin that is equal to or less than .25% of the total votes cast for or against the proposition, any 10 voters who voted in the election where the proposition was on the ballot may file a request for a recount
The voters requesting a recount under Subsection (7)(a) or (b) shall pay the costs of the recount.

recounts.note: Subsections (7)(a) and (b) give the trigger and subsection (10) the cost.

notes: Read in full: 20A-4-304 (declaration of results, 'tie vote'), 20A-4-306 (statewide canvass), 20A-4-401 (recounts), 20A-1-303 and 20A-1-304 (determining results; tie votes), and Part 3 (Presidential Electors) of chapter 13. Not read: chapter 9 (candidate nominating procedures; any primary-specific rule), 20A-1-404 (election controversies), the election contest part of chapter 4 beyond what says nothing of ties.
A recount here is 'all ballots cast in the race' recounted; 20A-4-401 has no recount for the requester's own cost beyond the margin and no waiver.

Utah's site draws a chapter's text by script, so the chapter PDFs linked under 'Download Options' were used, a documented download. The chapter page's address for the PDF is printed in the page's own link list.
